name: site_resolved_chemical_fields
hypothesis: Stability-related signals depend on how electronegativity and size contrast are distributed among realized local environments, not only their composition-wide or bond-wide averages. Balanced site fields and chemically disassortative contacts may capture network organization, while concentrated ionic load or strain-coupled contrast may mark heterogeneous environments.
scope: Periodic neighbor edges through 6 A, smoothly weighted by exp(-(d/(1.20*(r_cov,i+r_cov,j)))^6). Pauling electronegativity is used only when finite; radius mismatch uses covalent radii. Site fields are normalized by smooth site coordination with denominator floor 1e-6.
falsification: Falsified if neither formation MAE nor hull logloss improves over raw30 on adaptive validation. If train loss improves but validation degrades, the site heterogeneity summaries are treated as overfit; if only one task gains, scope is narrowed to that task.
